name: Joshua Rotenberg
body: The hard part you describe, getting AI to work inside a real field operation, is the problem I spend my days on. At Solenzo I design and tune automation and LLM-based agents for home-services businesses (electrical, plumbing, HVAC): lead capture, qualification, booking, reminders, no-show recovery, and follow-up. Those operators look a lot like your movers. Crews in the field, a phone that has to get answered, and an owner who wants results this quarter, not next year.

The work maps closely to what this role asks for. I decide where an agent takes the work and where a person stays in the loop, then review what the agents actually produce and tune until it holds up (I also built the rubric-based grading criteria my SEO audit process is scored against). When an integration breaks I go into it myself, in Zapier, Make, or n8n code steps, or SQL against the data. On the account side, I led an onboarding team of up to 20 at Wix while personally launching 25+ clients a month at 110% of implementation targets, built sequenced implementation plans and advised C-suite clients at Accelo, and retained roughly 94% of a 15 to 20 partner reseller network at Birdeye by catching adoption gaps early and feeding structured input back to Product.

Owning an account from signature through first renewal, and proving the ROI with data before anyone asks, is the kind of role I do my best work in. I'd welcome the chance to walk through how I'd plan an enterprise rollout in the case exercise.
